thread_title: S. flava var. maxima Berkeley Co, SC
breadcrumb: S. flava var. maxima Berkeley Co, SC

posts.body_html:
Yet another interesting clone of S. flava var. maxima from Berkeley Co, SC. One really neat feature of S. flava var. maxima is that under optimal conditions, the traps can appear to be almost neon yellow (although this one photographed below just has a yellow tinge to it). This particular clone is shapely and symmetrical with a moderately thin "neck." This is a new addition to the collection, so I don't know much about its growth habits other than it seems pretty easy and fast growing so far.

posts.body_html: Not sure which clone it is exactly, but I got a Berkeley Co maxima from Mike a few years back. Not only is it gorgeous, but it’s incredibly vigorous and makes TONS of pitchers straight into autumn! It’s my only flava that makes high quality pitchers continuously for that long. Here’s summer 2020 versus summer 2023 (specifically, today—note the new pitchers still coming up). I left all the senescing pitchers on just so you can get a sense of the sheer quantity produced (and not at all out of laziness…)
